Research task, as of 2026. Use WebSearch and WebFetch against official developer documentation (discord.com/developers, developers.facebook.com, learn.microsoft.com/linkedin) to answer precisely. Do NOT guess — cite the doc URL for each answer. I need to know whether a web app can programmatically VERIFY that a signed-in user follows/joined a specific brand account on each platform.

1. DISCORD. Confirm the exact current OAuth2 details for checking whether the authorizing user is a member of a specific guild:
   - The authorize URL, token URL, and token-exchange parameters.
   - The `identify` and `guilds` scopes: what does GET https://discord.com/api/v10/users/@me/guilds return, and does it include the guild id? Is there a `guilds.members.read` scope and a GET /users/@me/guilds/{guild.id}/member endpoint? Which is the better fit for "is this user in our guild"?
   - Rate limits / pagination caveats on /users/@me/guilds (default page size, `with_counts`).
   - What the /users/@me response looks like (field names for the user's snowflake id and username).

2. INSTAGRAM. Is there ANY current Meta API that lets an app determine whether a given Instagram user follows a specific Instagram account? Cover: Instagram Basic Display API (deprecation status), Instagram Graph API / Instagram API with Instagram Login, Business Discovery, and any `follows`/`followers` edges. State clearly whether the "does user X follow account Y" check is possible for a normal app, and what App Review/permission barriers exist.

3. FACEBOOK. Same question for "does this user LIKE our Facebook Page". Cover the `user_likes` permission and the `/me/likes/{page-id}` edge: does it still exist, what Graph API version changes affected it, and is it obtainable via App Review for a rewards/incentive use case? Also note Meta's Platform Policy stance on incentivizing likes/follows (there is a policy about not incentivizing Likes — find it and quote the relevant clause briefly).

4. LINKEDIN. Is there any LinkedIn API (Marketing Developer Platform, Community Management API, Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect) that reveals whether a member follows a given Company Page? What does Sign In with LinkedIn / OIDC actually return? Note any follower-statistics endpoints and whether they are aggregate-only.

Report back concisely: per platform, VERIFIABLE / NOT VERIFIABLE, the specific reason, and the doc URLs. Also flag any platform whose terms would prohibit incentivizing follows with rewards.

# Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect - LinkedIn | Microsoft Learn

## Overview

We are now offering a way for your apps to authenticate members using OpenID Connect.

## What is OpenID Connect

OpenID Connect (OIDC) is an identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0, enabling applications to authenticate members and obtain lite profile information about the member. OIDC will simplify the partner integration onboarding experience and eliminate dependencies on making additional API calls to find who the authenticated member is.

Note

Keep in mind Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect does not verify user identities and should not be marketed as such.

## Getting Started

### Authenticating Members

New members logging in to your service for the first time will need to follow the [Authenticating with OAuth 2.0 Guide](../../../shared/authentication/authentication?context=linkedin/consumer/context). When requesting the authorization code in Step 2 of the OAuth 2.0 Guide, make sure you use the OpenID scope `openid` to get the ID Token. We are also introducing new scopes `profile` and `email`.

| Permission Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| openid | Required to indicate the application wants to use OIDC to authenticate the member. |
| profile | Required to retrieve the member's lite profile including their id, name, and profile picture. |
| email | Required to retrieve the member's email address. |

After successful authentication, you will receive the member's access token and ID token.

If your application does not have these permissions provisioned, you can request access through the [Developer Portal](https://www.linkedin.com/developers/). Select your app from [My Apps](https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps), navigate to the Products tab, and request the Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect product.

### Retrieving Member Profiles Using ID Tokens

The primary extension that OIDC adds to OAuth 2.0 is enabling members to be Authenticated using the ID Token data structure. The ID Token is a security token that contains Claims about the Authentication of a member by an Authorization Server when using a Client, and potentially other requested Claims. The ID Token is represented as a JSON Web Token (JWT). With OIDC, you are now able to extract the member details from the ID Token.

##### ID Token Payload

| Permission Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| iss | The authorization server’s Identifier of the response https://www.linkedin.com |
| sub | User identifier |
| aud | client\_id of Relying party/caller Application guarantees user authentication for itself. |
| iat | ID Token issue time |
| exp | This is the expiration time of the token. The relying party processing this token should reject it once the expiration time is reached. |

#### Validating ID Tokens

ID Tokens can be validated using the metadata provided by [discovery document](https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/.well-known/openid-configuration) which contains OAuth endpoints, public keys and claims.

```JSON
{
    "issuer": "https://www.linkedin.com",
    "authorization_endpoint": "https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization",
    "token_endpoint": "https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken",
    "userinfo_endpoint": "https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo",
    "jwks_uri": "https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/openid/jwks",
    "response_types_supported": [
        "code"
    ],
    "subject_types_supported": [
        "pairwise"
    ],
    "id_token_signing_alg_values_supported": [
        "RS256"
    ],
    "scopes_supported": [
        "openid",
        "profile",
        "email"
    ],
    "claims_supported": [
        "iss",
        "aud",
        "iat",
        "exp",
        "sub",
        "name",
        "given_name",
        "family_name",
        "picture",
        "email",
        "email_verified",
        "locale"
    ]
}
```

[JWKS_URI](https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/openid/jwks) provided in the discovery document, can be used for signature verification.

#### API Request to retreive member details

In addition to the JWT received, you can also call userinfo endpoint to retrieve the member details.

```HTTP
GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo
Authorization: Bearer <access token>
```

#### Response Body Schema

| Field Name | Description | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sub | Subject Identifier | Text |
| name | Full name | Text |
| given\_name | Member's first name | Text |
| family\_name | Member's last name | Text |
| picture | Member's profile picture URL | Text |
| locale | Member's locale | Text |
| email | Member's primary e-mail address. **Optional** | Text |
| email\_verified | Indicator that Member's primary email has been verified. **Optional** | Boolean |

Note

The 'email' and 'email\_verified' fields are optional and may not be included in all responses. Ensure your application can handle cases where these fields are absent.

#### Sample API Response

```JSON
{
    "sub": "782bbtaQ",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "given_name": "John",
    "family_name": "Doe",
    "picture": "https://media.licdn-ei.com/dms/image/C5F03AQHqK8v7tB1HCQ/profile-displayphoto-shrink_100_100/0/",
    "locale": "en-US",
    "email": "doe@email.com",
    "email_verified": true
}
```

With the member's profile information successfully retrieved, the sign-in process is now complete and your member can continue to enjoy their personalized experience with your site or application.

# Discord OAuth2 Key Information

**Authorize URL:**
`https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize`

**Token URL:**
`https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token`

**Token Exchange POST Parameters:**
- `grant_type` (must be `authorization_code`)
- `code` (from querystring)
- `redirect_uri` (associated with authorization)

**Content-Type:** `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`

**Selected OAuth2 Scopes:**

| Scope | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| identify | "allows [`/users/@me`](/developers/resources/user#get-current-user) without `email`" |
| email | "enables [`/users/@me`](/developers/resources/user#get-current-user) to return an `email`" |
| guilds | "allows [`/users/@me/guilds`](/developers/resources/user#get-current-user-guilds) to return basic information about all of a user's guilds" |
| guilds.join | "allows [`/guilds/{guild.id}/members/{user.id}`](/developers/resources/guild#add-guild-member) to be used for joining users to a guild" |
| guilds.members.read | "allows [`/users/@me/guilds/{guild.id}/member`](/developers/resources/user#get-current-user-guild-member) to return a user's member information in a guild" |

# Discord User Resource Extraction

## (1) User Object Field Names

The core identifier fields are:
- **id**: snowflake type
- **username**: string type
- **global_name**: optional string type
- **discriminator**: string type
- **avatar**: optional string type

## (2) Get Current User Guilds

**Full URL:** `GET /users/@me/guilds`

**Required OAuth2 Scope:** `guilds`

**Query Parameters:**
- `before` (snowflake, optional): retrieve guilds preceding a specified guild ID
- `after` (snowflake, optional): retrieve guilds following a specified guild ID
- `limit` (integer, optional): defaults to 200, maximum of 200 guilds per request
- `with_counts` (boolean, optional): when enabled, includes approximate member and presence counts

**Example Partial Guild Object Fields:**
```
id, name, icon, banner, owner, permissions, features, 
approximate_member_count, approximate_presence_count
```

## (3) Get Current User Guild Member

**Full URL:** `GET /users/@me/guilds/{guild.id}/member`

**Required OAuth2 Scope:** `guilds.members.read`

**Returns:** "a [guild member](/developers/resources/guild#guild-member-object) object for the current user"

## Organization Follower Statistics API

The organizationalEntityFollowerStatistics API allows you to retrieve both lifetime and time-bound statistics on followers for an organization.

### Lifetime vs. Time-Bound Statistics

To retrieve lifetime follower statistics, omit the timeIntervals query parameter. The API returns follower counts segmented by various facets such as geo location and industry.

To retrieve time-bound follower statistics, include the timeIntervals query parameter. The API returns the aggregate follower count for both paid and organic followers during the days, weeks or months of the selected date range, based on the specified timeIntervals.timeGranularityType.

### Key Limitations

- The endpoint no longer returns totalFollowerCounts. Use the networkSizes API under Organization Lookup to retrieve an organization's total follower count.

- Time-bound follower counts are aggregated and not segmented by facet.

- Follower statistics can be broken down by 7 professional demographic facets. The results for any individual facet are limited to the top 100 results.

### Required Permissions

Your application will need to request the rw_organization_admin member permission in order for your application to successfully make API calls to this endpoint.

# Organization Lookup - LinkedIn | Microsoft Learn

Warning

**Deprecation Notice:** The Marketing Version 202508 (Marketing August 2025) will be sunset on August 17, 2026. We recommend that you migrate to the latest [versioned APIs](../../versioning) to avoid disruptions. For information on all the supported versions, refer to the [migrations](../../integrations/migrations#api-migration-status) documentation. If you haven’t yet migrated and have questions, submit a request on the [LinkedIn Developer Support Portal](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/ask/dsapi).

[![Try in Postman](../../../media/postman-button.png)](https://www.postman.com/linkedin-developer-apis/workspace/linkedin-marketing-solutions-versioned-apis/overview)

The Organization Lookup API searches organizations and their profiles.

Unless otherwise noted, the following rules apply when specifying input parameters:

- All strings are case-insensitive.
- Multiple words should be joined with a space. The input is URL encoded where spaces are translated to "%20". For example, Apple Inc. is encoded to `Apple%20Inc`.
- If a search includes multiple words, the complete string is searched.
- Wildcards and boolean logic ***are not supported***:
- `*`, `?`, `AND`, and `OR`

For information on finding organizations with partial or incomplete information, see the [Company Search](company-search) documentation.

## Permissions

| Permission | Description |
| --- | --- |
| rw\_organization\_admin | Manage organization pages and retrieve reporting data. |
| r\_compliance | Retrieve posts, comments, and likes on behalf of an authenticated member for compliance monitoring and archiving. This is a private permission and access is granted to select developers. |

Note

## Summary

| Platform | Verifiable? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Discord** | **VERIFIABLE** — cleanly | Purpose-built OAuth2 endpoint returns the user's membership in a named guild |
| **Instagram** | **NOT VERIFIABLE** | No follow-graph read exists in any current API; only aggregate counts |
| **Facebook** | **NOT VERIFIABLE in practice** | Endpoint exists, but `user_likes` App Review will not approve a rewards use case — and the policy forbids the use case outright |
| **LinkedIn** | **NOT VERIFIABLE** | All follower APIs are aggregate-only; OIDC returns identity only |

---

## 1. DISCORD — VERIFIABLE

**OAuth2 endpoints** ([docs.discord.com/developers/topics/oauth2](https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/oauth2) — `discord.com/developers/docs/topics/oauth2` now 301s here):

- Authorize: `https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize` (`client_id`, `response_type=code`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `state`)
- Token: `POST https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token`, `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
- Token-exchange body: `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `redirect_uri` (plus client credentials)

**Scopes** (verbatim from the scopes table):

- `identify` — "allows `/users/@me` without `email`"
- `email` — "enables `/users/@me` to return an `email`"
- `guilds` — "allows `/users/@me/guilds` to return basic information about all of a user's guilds"
- `guilds.members.read` — "allows `/users/@me/guilds/{guild.id}/member` to return a user's member information in a guild"

**Both endpoints exist** ([docs.discord.com/developers/resources/user](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/user)):

`GET /users/@me/guilds` (scope `guilds`) returns an array of **partial** guild objects — fields: `id`, `name`, `icon`, `banner`, `owner`, `permissions`, `features`, and with `with_counts=true` also `approximate_member_count` / `approximate_presence_count`. **Yes, it includes the guild `id`**, so a client-side `.some(g => g.id === GUILD_ID)` works.

`GET /users/@me/guilds/{guild.id}/member` (scope `guilds.members.read`) returns a **guild member object** for the current user in that specific guild.

**Better fit: `guilds.members.read`.** Reasons: one request, no pagination, non-membership surfaces as an error rather than requiring you to scan a list, it returns `roles` and `joined_at` (so you can gate on role or tenure, and detect join-then-leave gaming via `joined_at`), and the consent screen asks for access to *one* server rather than "see all your servers" — materially better conversion and privacy posture.

**Pagination / rate-limit caveats on `/users/@me/guilds`:**
- `limit` **defaults to 200, max 200**; `before` / `after` are snowflake cursors. 200 is also the non-Nitro guild cap, so one page usually suffices — but a Nitro user can exceed it, and *that is exactly when a naive single-page check produces a false negative*. This is the strongest practical argument for the member endpoint.
- Global limit is 50 req/s ([rate-limits](https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits)); per-route limits must be read from `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset-After` / `-Bucket`, not hardcoded.
- Caveat not in the official docs, so treat as unconfirmed: there are long-standing reports ([discord-api-docs#670](https://github.com/discord/discord-api-docs/issues/670)) that `/users/@me/*` buckets are shared across *different* user tokens rather than per-token, which bites backend OAuth services at volume. Worth load-testing.

**`/users/@me` response** — snowflake id is `id` (string), username is `username`; also `global_name` (the new display name), legacy `discriminator` (now `"0"` for migrated accounts), and `avatar`.

## 2. INSTAGRAM — NOT VERIFIABLE

- **Instagram Basic Display API: dead.** Deprecated **December 4, 2024**; all requests fail after that date ([announcement](https://developers.facebook.com/blog/post/2024/09/04/update-on-instagram-basic-display-api/)). Note that post also says there is no longer an Instagram API group for *consumer-facing* apps at all — which is precisely the category your use case falls into.
- **Instagram API with Instagram Login / with Facebook Login** ([overview](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/overview/)): permissions are `instagram_business_basic`, `instagram_business_content_publish`, `instagram_business_manage_comments`, `instagram_business_manage_messages` (+ `instagram_manage_insights`, `pages_show_list`, `pages_read_engagement` on the FB-Login variant). None expose a follow graph. These also authenticate *business/creator* accounts, not the ordinary consumer accounts your users would sign in with.
- **IG User node** ([reference](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/)): readable fields include `followers_count` and `follows_count` — **integers only**. There is **no `follows` / `followed_by` edge** returning which accounts are followed.
- **Business Discovery** ([docs](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-facebook-login/business-discovery/)): returns public metadata about *another* business account (`followers_count`, `media_count`, media). It is account-level, never per-relationship.
- **The one place a follow flag exists** is the Instagram Messaging **User Profile API** ([docs](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/messenger-platform/instagram/features/user-profile/)): fields `name, username, profile_pic, follower_count, is_user_follow_business, is_business_follow_user`. **It does not help you.** Consent is scoped to messaging: "A person sets user consent only when they send a message to your business, or click icebreakers or persistent menu." It is keyed on an IGSID from an existing conversation, requires `instagram_basic`, `instagram_manage_messages`, `pages_manage_metadata`, `pages_read_engagement` plus a Page token from someone with the MODERATE task. You cannot point it at an arbitrary web visitor who OAuth'd into your site.

**Verdict: "does user X follow account Y" is not answerable for a normal app.** No permission to apply for; the capability does not exist.

## 3. FACEBOOK — NOT VERIFIABLE IN PRACTICE

**The endpoint technically still exists.** `GET /v26.0/{user-id}/likes` is live in the current Graph API reference ([user/likes](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/reference/user/likes/)), returns a list of Page nodes with `created_time`, read-only, and takes a `target_id` parameter (the "target node") — which is the documented way to test one specific Page rather than paging the whole list.

**But the permission gate is the blocker.** `user_likes` ([permissions reference](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions/reference/user_likes)) requires App Review, and its **Allowed Usage** is enumerated narrowly: personalizing experiences by surfacing content matching user interests (content curation, sharing interests in dating/music apps), and parental-control/monitoring apps analyzing interests for safety concerns in under-18s. **A rewards or incentive gate is not among the approved use cases**, so a submission describing your actual use case should be expected to fail.

**Two further problems:**
1. Meta has moved Pages to the New Page Experience where **Followers replace Likes**. A Page under NPE may not have the Like signal you'd be querying at all.
2. `/{user-id}/likes` has always been prone to false negatives depending on the user's privacy settings — even when it works it is not a reliable gate.

**Policy — this is the real stopper.** Meta's developer policy on incentivization ([Platform Policy examples](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/apps/examples-platform-policy-4.4); fuller treatment at the [Incentivization Policies Deep Dive](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/terms-and-policies/incentivization-policy-deep-dive/), which currently 404s to automated fetches) permits incentivizing only a narrow set of actions — logging into your app with Facebook, checking in at your location, referral rewards for game installs — and **explicitly prohibits rewarding Page Likes or posting content**: don't incentivize people to post content to Facebook or Like a Page, or give the impression that doing so will be rewarded. The App Verification rejection guidance compresses this to: *"Only incentivize a person to log into your app or enter a promotion. Don't incentivize other actions."* Facebook's [Pages, Groups and Events Policies](https://www.facebook.com/policies/pages_groups_events/) reinforce it for promotions: a promotion must not require or incentivize participants to share, repost, or tag others.

**Note on sourcing:** several Meta policy pages returned Vietnamese-locale text or 404s to automated fetching. The clauses above are consistent across the pages that did resolve plus Meta's own search snippets, but I'd recommend one human read of the Incentivization Deep Dive page in a browser before you rely on the exact wording contractually.

## 4. LINKEDIN — NOT VERIFIABLE

**Sign In with LinkedIn / OIDC returns identity only** ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/consumer/integrations/self-serve/sign-in-with-linkedin-v2)). Scopes are exactly `openid`, `profile`, `email`. `GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo` returns: `sub`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `picture`, `locale`, `email`, `email_verified` (last two optional). Nothing about follows, connections, or company relationships. The docs also warn OIDC here "does not verify user identities and should not be marketed as such."

**All follower APIs are aggregate-only:**

- `organizationalEntityFollowerStatistics` ([docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/community-management/organizations/follower-statistics?view=li-lms-2026-08)) returns counts bucketed by 7 demographic facets (geo, industry, function, seniority, staff-count-range, association type), capped at top 100 results per facet. No member identities. Requires `rw_organization_admin`, restricted to authenticated ADMINISTRATORs of that page. It no longer returns `totalFollowerCounts`.
- `GET /rest/networkSizes/urn:li:organization:{id}?edgeType=COMPANY_FOLLOWED_BY_MEMBER` ([Organization Lookup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/community-management/organizations/organization-lookup-api?view=li-lms-2026-08)) returns exactly `{"firstDegreeSize": 219145}` — a single total. Despite the tempting edge-type name, it is a count, not a relationship test. (Version note: `CompanyFollowedByMember` → `COMPANY_FOLLOWED_BY_MEMBER` as of v202305, not backward compatible.)

There is no endpoint enumerating follower identities and none testing a specific member against a page. Also flag: Marketing Version 202508 sunsets **August 17, 2026** — under a week from now — so anything built here needs current versioning immediately.

## Policy flags for a rewards/incentive product

- **Facebook/Instagram: hard prohibition.** Incentivizing Page Likes is explicitly banned, and promotions may not require sharing/tagging. Since the technical capability is also absent on Instagram and gated behind an unapprovable review on Facebook, both platforms are closed to this feature on two independent grounds.
- **LinkedIn:** no incentivization clause surfaced in this research — but I did not audit the LinkedIn API Terms of Use or Professional Community Policies, so treat this as unresearched rather than cleared. Moot regardless, since the data isn't available.
- **Discord:** technically clean and I found no prohibition — but I did not review Discord's Developer Terms of Service or Developer Policy for incentivization language, so that should be checked before shipping. Worth noting Discord is the *only* platform of the four where this feature can be built at all.

**Practical recommendation:** build Discord verification with `identify` + `guilds.members.read` against `GET /users/@me/guilds/{guild.id}/member`, and for the other three platforms plan on an unverifiable honor-system or manual-proof flow — there is no API path to close that gap on any of them.
